Let me analyze this conflict.

Axis: applicant
- Register: "Keli Electric Manufacturing (Ningbo) Co., Ltd."
- Document: "Keli Sensing Technology (Ningbo) Co., Ltd."

Are these the same entity with spelling drift, or genuinely different names?

"Keli Electric Manufacturing" vs "Keli Sensing Technology" — these are quite different middle portions. "Electric Manufacturing" vs "Sensing Technology". The "(Ningbo) Co., Ltd." part matches.

In reality, Keli Sensing Technology (Ningbo) Co., Ltd. is a well-known load cell manufacturer (KELI). Keli Electric Manufacturing... Actually, I recall the actual OIML certificates for Keli are issued to "Keli Sensing Technology (Ningbo) Co., Ltd." KELI is a big load cell manufacturer in Ningbo. The document is the legal instrument, and the certificate itself says "Keli Sensing Technology (Ningbo) Co., Ltd."

Is "Keli Electric Manufacturing (Ningbo) Co., Ltd." an alternative English rendering of the same Chinese company? Possibly — Chinese companies sometimes have multiple English name translations. But the rule set: "Genuinely different company or person names = different-entity (best_value = the document's, since the certificate is the legal instrument)."

The core differentiator: "Electric Manufacturing" vs "Sensing Technology" — these describe different business activities, not spelling drift. It's not a legal-suffix drift, accent difference, or obvious OCR noise. So this looks like a genuinely different company name string. Per the rules, best_value = document's value.

Verdict: different-entity, best_value: "Keli Sensing Technology (Ningbo) Co., Ltd."

Why: The two names differ in their core business descriptors ("Electric Manufacturing" vs "Sensing Technology"), not merely in spelling/suffix drift, and the certificate document is the legal instrument.

One short sentence.
